name: BEVAN, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho parental choice tax credit is constitutional because Article IX, section 1 of the Idaho Constitution establishes a floor, not a ceiling, for legislative power regarding education, and the tax credit serves a public purpose by facilitating parental choice in educational services.

name: MOELLER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the decision clarifies the meaning of Article IX, section 1, affirming that the constitutional foundation for public education in Idaho remains intact and the legislature's duty to maintain public schools is fixed, while also assisting parents who choose education outside the public system.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that exterior sniffs of a vehicle by a drug dog are not searches under Article 1, Section 17 of the Idaho Constitution, and that Article 1, Section 17 does not impose a heightened standard for the automobile exception.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the FIS and short ballot title failed to substantially comply with Idaho law, necessitating revisions, but the long ballot title substantially complied.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Twin Falls City waste collection ordinance was not intended to promote privacy and did not create an objectively reasonable expectation of privacy in curbside garbage, affirming prior precedent.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho Parental Rights Act does not apply to private party guardianships, strict scrutiny is not required, Alayna waived her right to challenge certain statutes, other statutes are constitutional under rational basis review, Alayna was found to be an unfit parent, and the Murrays' actions did not warrant dismissal of the guardianship.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred in the result, but dissented from parts of the majority's analysis, arguing that the Idaho Parental Rights Act does apply to the guardianship statutes and that strict scrutiny should be applied, but that the statutes still survive strict scrutiny given Alayna's unfitness.

name: ZAHN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that while Article V, section 13 of the Idaho Constitution does not empower the legislature to mandate consecutive sentences, the power to do so was not exclusively reserved to the judiciary at common law, thus Idaho Code section 19-2520G(3) does not violate the separation of powers.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that House Bills 124 and 340 are reasonable exercises of the legislature's authority to enact conditions on the right of suffrage and do not violate the Idaho Constitution's equal protection clause, applying rational basis review.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 6-311A is constitutional but a tenant is entitled to a jury trial on legal claims raised through affirmative defenses in an unlawful detainer action.

name: ZAHN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the legislative preapproval requirement for pending fee rules is constitutional as rulemaking authority is a legislative delegation, not a constitutional power, and does not violate separation of powers, enactment, presentment, or Article III, section 29 of the Idaho Constitution.

name: STEGNER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the district court correctly found that Idaho Code section 67-3004(10) impinges on the Supreme Court's prerogative to make its own rules governing its procedure, thus affirming the district court's decision.

name: ZAHN
description: Concurred, argued that the district court correctly denied the motion to suppress and the objection to reduced peremptory challenges, as neither the Idaho nor U.S. Constitutions guarantee a specific number of peremptory challenges.

name: BEVAN, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Plaintiffs lacked standing because their alleged injuries (diminished property values, aesthetic/recreational interests, and membership value) were speculative, generalized, and lacked a fairly traceable causal connection to the proposed development, adhering to federal standing principles.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Idaho's constitution allows for broader standing than the restrictive federal standards adopted by the majority, and that Tidwell should have standing to challenge governmental conduct.

name: Bevan
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho Constitution prohibits warrantless arrests for completed misdemeanors unless the offense occurred in the arresting officer's personal presence, and collective knowledge cannot bypass this requirement.

name: Moeller
description: Dissented, argued that the collective knowledge doctrine should apply to misdemeanor arrests and that the majority's ruling unnecessarily hinders law enforcement's ability to protect the public.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the district court's judgment was affirmed in part and reversed in part, specifically reversing the ITCA bar on individual refunds for unconstitutional street impact fees but affirming other rulings.

name: STEGNER, JUSTICE.
description: Concurred, argued that the federal 4-R Act does not preempt Idaho's constitutional requirement for uniform property taxation, and that genuine issues of material fact exist regarding the equalization of operating property compared to other commercial property.

name: ZAHN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Pool's waiver of Fourth Amendment rights constituted consent to warrantless searches of her residence, and since Idaho's Article I, section 17 rights were coextensive in this instance, the search was lawful.

name: BRODY
description: Concurred, argued that the Idaho Constitution does not implicitly guarantee a fundamental right to abortion, as such a right is not "deeply rooted" in Idaho's history and traditions, and the challenged laws are rationally related to legitimate governmental purposes.

name: ZAHN, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Idaho Constitution's Inalienable Rights Clause implicitly protects a pregnant woman's fundamental right to obtain an abortion to preserve her life or health, based on the plain language, history, and traditions.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Idaho Constitution provides broader fundamental rights to women, including a fundamental right to obtain an abortion to protect their life, liberty, and safety, and that the majority's decision strips women of these basic rights.

name: MOELLER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the failure to comply with statutory arrest notice requirements does not constitute a constitutional violation that would warrant the suppression of evidence.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that a violation of Idaho Code section 19-608 constitutes an unlawful arrest and an unreasonable seizure under the Idaho Constitution, requiring suppression of evidence.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 20-1016 is constitutional because the 1986 amendment to Article IV, section 7 authorizes the legislature to govern the Commission's commutation powers, including gubernatorial review in death penalty cases.

name: HORTON, J. pro tem
description: Concurred in the result but argued that Idaho Code section 20-1016(2) is unconstitutional as it impermissibly reallocates the Commission's clemency authority to the governor, and that there is no effective statute authorizing the Commission to commute Pizzuto's sentence for murder.

name: Justice BRODY
description: Concurred with the result reached by the Court.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the combined 28 seconds of deviations did not actually lengthen the traffic stop because the drug dog alerted 48 seconds before the citations were completed, establishing reasonable suspicion for a new crime, thus not prolonging the overall detention beyond what the Fourth Amendment tolerates.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while he agrees with the result based on Fourth Amendment jurisprudence, he believes Idaho's constitution (Article I, section 17) should provide greater protection against dog sniff searches than the U.S. Constitution, requiring reasonable suspicion for such searches.

name: STEGNER, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that victims do not have standing in a criminal case to independently seek renewal of a judgment for an order of restitution, as criminal proceedings are between the State and the defendant.

name: STEGNER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Commission was organized on September 1, 2021, making the filing of the report timely, and that the statutory escape clause allows precinct splitting for both legislative and congressional redistricting plans.

name: STEGNER, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that petitioners failed to establish that Plan L03 was unconstitutional under federal and state law, as the Commission reasonably determined the necessary county divisions to comply with equal protection and rejected alternative plans as deficient.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Randall's Fourth Amendment rights were violated when the drug dog leapt inside his car without a warrant or consent, as this constituted an unconstitutional search for information.

name: STEGNER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the U.S. Supreme Court's Fourth Amendment jurisprudence is flawed by not classifying an exterior dog sniff as a search, and that the Idaho Constitution provides greater privacy protections, making any drug dog sniff a search.

name: BEVAN, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, argued that the drug dog's instinctive entry into the vehicle did not constitute police misconduct and therefore did not violate the Fourth Amendment, and that applying the exclusionary rule in such cases does not serve its purpose of deterring police.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Concurred with the ultimate decision but disagreed with the majority's reasoning on Gilmore's standing and the application of strict scrutiny.

name: BRODY, J.
description: Concurred that SB 1110 is unconstitutional but dissented from applying strict scrutiny, arguing a 'reasonable and workable' standard should be used instead.

name: BEVAN, Chief Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the warrantless arrest for a completed misdemeanor DUI was unlawful because the officer lacked sufficient personal knowledge at the time of arrest to establish probable cause for a felony, violating Amstutz's constitutional rights.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Sutterfield's arrest was a valid citizen's arrest, and the officer's failure to fully comply with statutory notice requirements did not constitute a constitutional violation warranting suppression of evidence.

name: STEGNER, J.
description: Dissented, argued that Sutterfield was unlawfully arrested when placed in handcuffs before the citizen's arrest was effectuated, and that the distinction between constitutional and statutory violations erodes protections against unreasonable searches and seizures.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Rule 41(f) does not require the return of contraband even if evidence was suppressed, and that the prohibition of marijuana does not violate constitutional religious liberty.

name: MOELLER, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 49-1405(1)(b) violates the Idaho Constitution by allowing warrantless arrests for misdemeanors committed outside an officer's presence, and that evidence obtained from an unlawful arrest is inadmissible in administrative license suspension hearings.

name: BRODY, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Idaho Code section 5-230 is constitutional, does not violate due process or equal protection rights, and equitable estoppel does not apply as SLRMC's statement was not a false representation of a past or existing fact.
